title: Containers and Kubernetes: could one compromised pod take over the cluster?
short: Make the API server private, enforce Pod Security baseline in every namespace and upgrade within each version's 12 months of patches.
answer: This month, take the API server off the internet, enforce the baseline Pod Security Standard in every namespace and start replacing Ingress NGINX, which has had no security fixes since March 2026[^r136]. Then judge every other setting by whether it stops one compromised pod from reaching its node, the cloud account or a more powerful service account.
audience: Platform, DevOps and security teams running Kubernetes on AKS, EKS, GKE or their own servers, from one cluster to many

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Take the API server off the internet.
items.text: EKS, AKS and GKE all expose it publicly by default[^eksendpoint][^aksapi][^gkeharden]. Use a private endpoint, or GKE's DNS-based endpoint, and allow only admin networks. Microsoft found that default credentials, exposed APIs and unpatched images drive most successful container compromises[^mddr].

items.title: Enforce Pod Security baseline in every namespace.
items.text: Label each namespace `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline`, which blocks privileged containers, hostPath volumes and host namespaces[^pss], and set `warn` and `audit` to `restricted`[^psa]. North Korea's UNC4899 broke out of a cluster through a pod running in privileged mode[^th].

items.title: Treat pod creation as a privileged right.
items.text: Anyone who can create pods in a namespace can mount its Secrets and run as any of its service accounts[^rbacgp]. Every quarter, list who holds that right, `cluster-admin` or the rights below, and cut the list.

items.title: Keep workload credentials short-lived.
items.text: Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` unless a pod calls the API[^appcheck], avoid non-expiring token Secrets[^checklist] and block pods from the node's cloud role[^eksbpiam]. UNC4899 stole database passwords from a pod's environment variables[^th].

items.title: Stay on a supported version, add-ons included.
items.text: Kubernetes patches only its three newest minor versions, each for about a year[^releases]. Ingress NGINX, used in about half of cloud native environments, can read every Secret by default and was retired on 24 March 2026[^ingstmt][^ingcve][^r136]. Replace unmaintained add-ons.

blocks.title: Harden a running cluster in this order

items.title: Who can reach and administer it?
items.text: List each cluster's endpoint, version, add-ons and `cluster-admin` bindings. Find Ingress NGINX with `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx`[^ingstmt].

items.title: Which pods would Pod Security reject?
items.text: Set `warn` and `audit` first. They also check Deployments, while `enforce` rejects only pods, so a bad Deployment is accepted and then never starts[^psa].

items.title: Does your network plugin enforce NetworkPolicy?
items.text: If not, a NetworkPolicy has no effect[^netpol]. Add default-deny ingress and egress policies to each namespace, then allow what you need, DNS included.

items.title: What does Pod Security miss?
items.text: Add admission rules for image sources and digests[^checklist]. ValidatingAdmissionPolicy is built in, stable since 1.30, and can `Warn` and `Audit` before it denies[^vap]. Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper are add-on alternatives[^pss].

items.title: Would you see a takeover?
items.text: Turn on audit logs: off by default on EKS[^ekslogs], behind a diagnostic setting on AKS[^aksmon] and, self-managed, off without `--audit-policy-file`[^auditing]. Alert on `exec` into pods, new cluster role bindings and Secrets listed by people.

blocks.title: Defaults to change on EKS, AKS and GKE

columns.title: Amazon EKS
items: **Public endpoint.** Enable private access, then limit or disable public access[^eksendpoint].
**No control plane logs.** Enable at least `audit` and `authenticator`[^ekslogs].
**aws-auth.** It is deprecated: move to access entries and drop `cluster-admin` from the cluster creator[^eksbpiam].
**Support.** 14 months, then 12 of paid extended support, on by default. It ends for 1.31 on 26 November 2026[^eksver].

columns.title: Azure AKS
items: **Public API server.** Use a private cluster or at least authorized IP ranges[^aksapi].
**Local accounts.** On by default, they are an unaudited way around Entra ID. Set `--disable-local-accounts` and rotate certificates[^akslocal].
**Audit logs.** Route `kube-audit-admin`, which skips get and list events and costs less[^aksmon].
**Support.** 12 months per version; 1.34 reaches end of life in November 2026[^aksver].

columns.title: Google GKE
items: **Reachable control plane.** Use only the DNS-based endpoint, or authorized networks[^gkeharden].
**Anonymous requests.** Set `--anonymous-authentication-config=LIMITED`; only clusters created on 1.35 deny them by default[^gkeharden].
**Upgrades.** Use a release channel with accelerated patch auto-upgrades[^gkeharden].
**Cloud access.** Use Workload Identity Federation, always on in Autopilot[^gkeharden].

blocks.title: RBAC rights that lead to cluster admin
items: **`list` or `watch` on Secrets.** Both return the Secrets' contents[^rbacgp].
**`escalate`, `bind` and `impersonate`.** They bypass RBAC's escalation checks or borrow another user's rights[^rbacgp].
**Any right on `nodes/proxy`.** Even `get` runs commands in every pod on the node, unaudited and past admission control[^rbacgp].
**Webhook configurations, `serviceaccounts/token` and PersistentVolumes.** They let the holder read admitted objects, mint tokens or mount the node's disk[^rbacgp].
**`patch` on namespaces.** It lets a user relabel a namespace to a looser Pod Security level[^rbacgp].

blocks.title: Pod settings that stop an escape
items: **Non-root, no escalation.** Restricted requires `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, a seccomp profile and dropping `ALL` capabilities[^pss].
**Read-only root filesystem.** Set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`[^appcheck]. Restricted doesn't require it[^pss], so add an admission rule.
**User namespaces.** Since 1.36, `hostUsers: false` maps container root to an unprivileged host user[^userns].
**Minimal images by digest.** No shells or debug tools, and sha256 digests instead of tags[^checklist]. Signing is in the supply-chain sheet.
**Secrets as files.** Environment variables leak more easily than mounted files; mount secrets from an external store with the Secrets Store CSI Driver[^checklist].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Ingress NGINX is archived.** It gets no fixes after 24 March 2026[^r136]. Move to Gateway API or another Ingress controller[^ingstmt].

**Kubernetes 1.36 closed old gaps.** It disabled `gitRepo` volumes for good, deprecated Service `externalIPs` and made user namespaces and fine-grained kubelet authorization generally available[^r136].
**Admission policies can live on disk.** Manifest-based admission control, beta in 1.37, enforces policies from API server startup and can protect them from privileged API users[^r137].
**AKS will upgrade unsupported clusters itself.** From 1 June 2027, 60 days after end of support, ignoring maintenance windows and deprecated API checks[^akspiu].

**Linux root exploits came with public code.** Three flaws disclosed from 29 April to 13 May 2026 gave local users root on major distributions[^mddr]. Patch node images within the patching sheet's deadlines.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A service mesh just for encryption.** The checklist suggests one only if your network plugin can't encrypt traffic[^checklist].
**Waiting for fixes to old CVEs.** Scanners can flag CVE-2020-8561, CVE-2020-8562 and CVE-2021-25740 on every version since June 2026; they won't be fixed[^unfixed]. Mitigate once and accept them.
**CPU limits on every pod.** They throttle work and can upset autoscaling; the checklist suggests them only for sensitive workloads[^checklist].
**Sandboxed runtimes everywhere.** Keep gVisor or Kata Containers for untrusted or sensitive code[^appcheck].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Exempting a controller from Pod Security.** Exempting the ReplicaSet controller exempts everyone who can create a Deployment[^psa].
**Binding roles to built-in groups.** `system:unauthenticated` is anyone who can reach the API server[^rbacgp]; on GKE, `system:authenticated` includes any Google account[^gkeharden].
**Keeping bindings for deleted users.** A new account with the same name inherits them[^rbacgp].
**Upgrading the control plane but not the nodes.** EKS node groups don't follow it[^eksver].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Prefer a managed mode with secure defaults: GKE Autopilot disallows privileged pods[^th].
Limit the API server to your VPN or office addresses, and turn on audit logs.
Label every namespace `enforce: baseline` and turn on automatic patch upgrades.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Reach a private API server through a VPN or bastion, with SSO groups mapped to RBAC roles.
Keep admission and network policies in Git, and move each rule from warn to deny.
Upgrade the minor version twice a year, staging cluster first.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Give each trust level its own cluster: Kubernetes calls namespace boundaries weak[^rbacgp].
On self-managed clusters, load must-have admission policies from disk[^r137].
Send audit logs and runtime alerts from GuardDuty, Defender for Containers or Falco to the SIEM.
